question:
**Case Study 5: Linear Systems in Market Analysis**

A start-up sells two subscription types, Basic and Premium. Each month, their marketing manager collects data on the number of campaigns required ($x$) and funds spent ($y$) to achieve the targets. The system

$$\begin{cases}2x + 3y = 14 \\ 5x + 4y = 23\end{cases}$$

is formed for a particular analysis.

(a) Write this system in matrix form $AX=B$.
(b) Find the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A$.
(c) Solve for $x$ and $y$ using the matrix inverse method.
(d) Verify your solution by direct substitution.
explanation:
(a) The system is:

$\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 14 \\ 23 \end{bmatrix}$

$A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$, $X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}$, $B = \begin{bmatrix} 14 \\ 23 \end{bmatrix}$

(b)

$|A| = 2*4 - 3*5 = 8 - 15 = -7 \ne 0$

$A$ is invertible.

$A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-7} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -3 \\ -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

(c) $X = A^{-1} B = \dfrac{1}{-7} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -3 \\ -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 14 \\ 23 \end{bmatrix}$

First row: $4\times14 + (-3)\times23 = 56 - 69 = -13$

Second row: $-5\times14 + 2\times23 = -70 + 46 = -24$

$X = \dfrac{1}{-7} \begin{bmatrix} -13 \\ -24 \end{bmatrix}$

$ = \begin{bmatrix} 13/7 \\ 24/7 \end{bmatrix}$

Thus, $x = 13/7$, $y = 24/7$.

(d)

Check in first equation:

$2x + 3y = 2 \times \dfrac{13}{7} + 3 \times \dfrac{24}{7} = \dfrac{26 + 72}{7} = \dfrac{98}{7} = 14$ ✓

Second equation:

$5x + 4y = 5 \times \dfrac{13}{7} + 4 \times \dfrac{24}{7} = \dfrac{65 + 96}{7} = \dfrac{161}{7} = 23$ ✓

options.A:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&5\\3&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}14\\23\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $A^{-1}=\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}4&-3\\-5&2\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) $x=\frac{24}{7}$, $y=\frac{13}{7}$.
(d) Substitution does not satisfy both equations.
options.B:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\5&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}23\\14\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $A$ is singular.
(c) No unique solution exists.
(d) Verification is not possible.
